I will keep my land mainly in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation, because that is still the most reliable way for me to use my fields efficiently in Quzhou County. Our area suits this double-cropping system, I know its management well, and it gives me stable grain output with manageable risk. Since I am educated and I want dependable results rather than experimenting widely, I will use improved or hybrid seed, control fertilizer more precisely, irrigate at the key growth stages, and keep pesticides limited to necessary applications based on field pressure. For wheat, I will focus on strong early growth, disease prevention, and water at overwintering, jointing, and grain filling if conditions require it. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly to protect yield, use hybrid seed, emphasize nitrogen and potassium support, and irrigate at the critical stages if rainfall is short. I will use rotary tillage for the wheat season after maize residue handling, and mostly no-tillage or light tillage before summer maize so I can save time and moisture. This is the plan I would follow because it matches local climate, my experience, and my goal of stable production with controlled input costs.
